title: Double-tap by touchpad on the titlebar doesn't maximize/unmaximize the window in GNOME 44, Wayland
body:
### System

OS: Arch
Version: alacritty 0.13.0-dev (ea2c39e6)
Linux/BSD: Wayland session on GNOME 44

Double-tap by touchpad on the titlebar doesn't maximize/unmaximize the window.

Instead triple-tap maximizes/unmaximized the window.

Mouse double-click works.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: How fast do you tap? There's no difference between touchpad and mouse from the Wayland protocol point of view, so it's a matter of speed when it comes to touchpad double tap.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
That's could be related to #6983. 
I tried to check this behavior on my machine, something is weird and it's going on. But I am starting to think this is GNOME 44...
### What I mean ###
While double-tapping did not work for me, double-_clicking_ did. (and tripple-tapping to)
My speed is somewhere around 125~300ms on average.(7.78 in a second) So it should be plenty.
Double-tapping transforms cursor to move alacritty window. Same can be done with _one_ click.

### System ###
OS: Ubuntu 23.04 (Lunar Lobster)
Version: alacritty 0.12.1
Linux/BSD: Wayland with GNOME 44

### Window ###
Default config.

comments.body:
Let's start with the libinput logs This should account for end, but in the `li-events.log` the ind is within 20-30ms, so it doesn't matter, since it's still in 250ms ranges.
```
-event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +0.215s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +1.368s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +1.531s	1 // Double tap here
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +2.613s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +2.798s	1 // Double tap here
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +3.823s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +4.008s	1 // Double tap here
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +4.200s	1 // Triple tap
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +5.403s	1

 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +10.214s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +11.132s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +12.754s	1
 event11  GESTURE_HOLD_BEGIN      +13.651s	1
```

For me it looks more or less good, however let's now see what we've got on the wayland side, for grep '<email-scrubbed>|move|maximize`.

```
[1135579.263] <email-scrubbed>(2744, 907047, 272, 1)
[1135579.328]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2744)
[1144375.881] <email-scrubbed>(2761, 915854, 272, 1)
[1144375.918]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2761)
[1145720.100] <email-scrubbed>(2768, 917182, 272, 1)
[1145720.135]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2768)
[1146965.425] <email-scrubbed>(2775, 918427, 272, 1)
[1146965.460]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2775)
[1148190.285] <email-scrubbed>(2782, 919637, 272, 1)
[1148190.320]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2782)
[1148588.580] <email-scrubbed>(2787, 920014, 272, 1)
[1148588.621]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2787)
[1149762.438] <email-scrubbed>(2794, 921217, 272, 1)
[1149762.479]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2794)
[1150146.699] <email-scrubbed>(2799, 921580, 272, 1)
[1150146.769]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2799)
[1151278.781] <email-scrubbed>(2806, 922725, 272, 1)
[1151278.814]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2806)
[1151641.759] <email-scrubbed>(2811, 923102, 272, 1)
[1151641.847]  -> <email-scrubbed>(wl_seat@8, 2811)
[1154566.434] <email-scrubbed>(2828, 926028, 272, 1)
[1154746.590] <email-scrubbed>(2829, 926084, 272, 0)
[1154746.642]  -> <email-scrubbed>_maximized()
[1157114.567] <email-scrubbed>(2850, 928568, 272, 1)
[1157293.811] <email-scrubbed>(2851, 928631, 272, 0)
[1157293.859]  -> <email-scrubbed>_maximized()
```

We're interested in `<email-scrubbed>` events, where they hava `1` at the end, the `1` means pressed. The second argument here is a timestamp of the events with milliseconds granularity, so by doing a `diff` between the ones adjustment ones we'll get the time between you've clicked. I'd say before that we don't rely on such a thing internally and we just use the current timestamp when we've seen event during event processing. But let's just compute the differences in time between those events.

```
[1135579.263] <email-scrubbed>(2744, 907047, 272, 1)
[1144375.881] <email-scrubbed>(2761, 915854, 272, 1) // 8 seconds 
[1145720.100] <email-scrubbed>(2768, 917182, 272, 1) // 1328ms 
[1146965.425] <email-scrubbed>(2775, 918427, 272, 1) // 1245ms
[1148190.285] <email-scrubbed>(2782, 919637, 272, 1) // 1210 ms
[1148588.580] <email-scrubbed>(2787, 920014, 272, 1) // 377ms double click
[1149762.438] <email-scrubbed>(2794, 921217, 272, 1) // 1203ms
[1150146.699] <email-scrubbed>(2799, 921580, 272, 1) // 363ms double click
[1151278.781] <email-scrubbed>(2806, 922725, 272, 1) // 1145
[1151641.759] <email-scrubbed>(2811, 923102, 272, 1) // 377 ms , double click
[1154566.434] <email-scrubbed>(2828, 926028, 272, 1) // 3s
[1154746.642]  -> <email-scrubbed>_maximized()
```

If you see on the wayland logs, the time between the clicks when you did double clicks were very close to 400ms. On libinput logs the time between the clicks were 150ms-200ms, this is for example what I have in wayland logs on sway and it matches libinput results on my end.

For now though, I'll try to rewrite and use the timestamps directly from the events, since they might provide better results. I'll come back to you with that eventually.

The issue is what gnome does now and that it doesn't work with some policies of handling double clicks. In this case the issue is gnome bug, but we could work around it by changing the way we react to clicking on decorations and starting the move.
